items.text: SEASON 8 · EPISODE 1 · DRAFT · CASE-040  A live build · Maya, Kit, Bram, Odile and Nkechi · Level L5 · Advanced support (formulas on request)  The Wyndmere Centre for the Performing Arts tops out. Fourteen weeks to a sold-out preview — and the backbone is in the wrong wall.  ⚑ RV-160: the general contractor owns sequence; Maya directs no trade. RV-162: hard hats and hi-vis on site; nobody works at height in the story. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: Topping Out
items.stakes: The last beam is up. The backbone is in — through a wall that's coming down on Tuesday.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #72 · AVERY'S LENS  A change reaches everyone it touches  A drawing change is only real for the people who received it. Distribution is part of the design.  Bulletin 14 moved a wall. The low-voltage contractor never got it, and pulled the backbone through the wall that was about to be demolished.

items.alt: A plan sheet of level 1: the MER on the left, the stage rack on the right; the backbone drawn in red straight through the east dock wall, marked B14; a grey dashed north riser route (390 m, 2.44 dB margin) and a grey dashed south pathway on the drawings (300 m, 4.28 dB margin).
items.caption: Pulled neatly. Through the wrong wall.

items.prompt: 14:00. The dock bay is demolished on Tuesday. How do you raise it?
items.happening: Backbone in the east dock wall.
unknown: Why the LV sub used the old wall
items.risk: A new backbone destroyed — or a trade directed around its contractor.
timeout: The afternoon goes to another meeting.
Monday's lookahead still shows the dock bay demolition on Tuesday.

hints.text: Who owns the sequence — and why didn't this trade know?

options.label: Tell the low-voltage sub's foreman to re-pull tonight
options.fail: Trades are directed by the general contractor.

options.label: RFI through Odile to the GC: the backbone is in a wall Bulletin 14 demolishes — hold that bay until a reroute is agreed — and ask why the low-voltage sub built to the old set
options.result: Bram holds the bay two days; his document controller goes quiet, then finds the gap.
options.consequence: Through the contract chain, with the question behind the problem.

options.label: Let demolition cut it; re-pull later
options.result: The stage rack loses three weeks of commissioning.
options.consequence: Destroys work to avoid a conversation.

options.label: Ask Odile to keep the old wall
options.result: Odile: “The truck bay is the owner's requirement.”

items.title: Bulletin 14.
items.body: Bulletin 14 moved the east dock wall two metres for a bigger truck bay. Its transmittal went to eleven trades — electrical, mechanical, drywall, doors, steel. The low-voltage subcontractor joined the job a week later and was never added. They pulled a clean, labelled, tested backbone straight through the old wall.
items.label: Test: why did they use the old wall — and whose gap is it?

items.sub: Advanced · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Maya and Kit beside a board. South pathway: three hundred metres of single-mode, two connectors, one splice. What does it lose — and is that enough margin? Point three kilometres at point four is point one two; connectors one point five; splice point three. One point nine two — four point two eight under the six point two budget. The spec asks for three. The north riser leaves two point four. The spare pathway on the drawings was the answer all along.

items.text: 📙 ON REQUEST · ADVANCED  Terms   Backbone   Single-mode fiber   Optical loss budget   Architect's bulletin   If you need it   ƒ Ask for the formula · Optical loss budget   ƒ FORMULA · Optical loss budget  L = α × d + n c  × L c  + n s  × L s  · margin = budget − L   α  fiber attenuation, dB/km  d  length, km  n c , L c   mated connector pairs and the loss allowed for each, dB  n s , L s   splices and the loss allowed for each, dB  budget  the transceiver's allowed channel loss, dB      ƒ Ask for the formula · Losses in dB add   ƒ FORMULA · Losses in dB add  P rx  = P clear  − L 1  − L 2  − …   P clear   level with a clear path, dBm  L 1 , L 2   each loss, dB

items.label: **Learn it now:** backbones, loss budgets and bulletins.

items.title: Glass clear enough to talk through
items.body: In 1970 a team of three researchers drew the first optical fiber that lost less than 20 decibels per kilometre — the threshold engineers had said would make light a practical way to carry calls. Today's single-mode fiber loses about 0.4 dB per kilometre at 1310 nm. The budget arithmetic hasn't changed; the glass has.

items.title: The spare pathway.
items.body: The obvious reroute is up the north riser: 390 metres, four connectors, two splices — 3.76 dB against the optics' 6.2 dB budget, leaving 2.44 dB. The spec asks for 3. Kit, digging in last year's set, finds sheet T-101: a south pathway, two empty 50 mm conduits, drawn for backbone diversity — 300 metres, two connectors, one splice. 1.92 dB. 4.28 of margin.
items.label: Test: which route meets the spec's margin?
**Work it out:** choose the backbone route the building will keep.

items.prompt: Friday. Which route goes in the RFI answer?
unknown: Whether the south conduits are clear
items.risk: A backbone that fails its first dirty connector.
timeout: The RFI answer slips to Tuesday.
The demolition crew arrives at a wall with a backbone in it.

hints.text: Which route meets the spec's margin — and how will you prove it?

options.label: The north riser — it's open and quick
options.result: It passes the budget and misses the spec's margin by 0.56 dB.

options.label: The south pathway on the drawings: single-mode, one splice at the south pull box — with the loss calculation attached, and an OTDR trace and loss test witnessed by Nkechi
options.result: The LV sub pulls it Monday; Nkechi witnesses 1.98 dB measured against 1.92 calculated.
options.consequence: The route the design promised, with the numbers and the proof.

options.label: Multimode on the south route — cheaper optics
options.consequence: Cheap today, dark after the first dirty connector.

options.label: A wireless bridge between the MER and the stage
options.result: A performance venue's backbone on a radio link across a steel building.

items.alt: The same plan after the fix: the old path through the dock wall greyed out; the south pathway drawn in heavy green, 300 m, 4.28 dB of margin; below: pulled south, OTDR and loss test witnessed.
items.caption: The route the drawings promised.

items.prompt: Your cable's in my wall. My demolition crew starts Tuesday. Not my problem.

options.label: “It's both of ours. I'll get you an RFI answer by Monday with a route and the numbers — can you hold that bay two days while it's pulled?”
options.reply: Two days. Get me paper by Monday and I'll move the crew to the west bay.

options.label: “Your document control missed a trade.”
options.reply: Maybe. Blame later. What do you need?

options.label: “Just have your guys work around it.”
options.reply: Around a cable in a wall I'm knocking down? No.

items.title: distribution: 11 trades
items.body: Bulletin 14's transmittal: eleven trades on the distribution list. Electrical, mechanical, drywall, doors, the steel erector… The low-voltage subcontractor joined the job a week later and was never added.

items.prompt: Monday's OAC meeting. How do bulletins reach every trade from now on?
known: ◉ LV sub missing from the list
items.risk: The next bulletin building the old building.
timeout: The meeting runs out of time.
Bulletin 17 goes out on the old list.

hints.text: Who owns distribution — and how would you know it worked?

options.label: Email every bulletin to everyone on the project
options.result: Three hundred people, twelve bulletins a week, nobody reads them.

options.label: The GC's document control keeps a distribution matrix — each bulletin goes to every trade it touches and each acknowledges — and the design team checks the matrix at every OAC meeting
options.result: Bram's document controller adds the LV sub and two others who'd joined late.
options.consequence: Fix the gap between trades, not just the cable.

options.label: You email the LV sub directly from now on
options.result: The contract says the GC transmits. Two versions of the truth.
options.consequence: Bypasses the chain you just used.

options.label: Nothing — it was a one-off
options.result: Bulletin 17 misses the fire alarm sub.
options.fail: A gap that swallowed one trade will swallow another.

items.body: Sheet T-101 from last year's design set: a dashed line along the south corridor, labelled ‘SPARE PATHWAY · 2 × 50 mm conduit · for backbone diversity’. Installed, empty, waiting.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  A change is only real for the people who received it: bulletins go to every trade they touch, and the general contractor owns that distribution. Fiber loss adds in dB — L = α·d + n c ·L c  + n s ·L s  — and the spec’s margin is a requirement, not a wish. Prove a link with an OTDR trace and a witnessed loss test. Raise problems through the contract chain; never direct a trade yourself.
REFLECTION (optional)  · Think of a change at your work. Who needed to know about it — and how would you know they did?
